Ask a Global Reader to read the TAP code from the user's profile
Wait for the system to email the TAP value to the user automatically
Create a new TAP and record its value immediately, because the value cannot be viewed again after creation

explanation: Correct: the TAP value is shown once when created and cannot be viewed again after selecting OK — the admin must make a note of it at creation. The other options invent a recovery path that does not exist: TAP values are not stored retrievably, not emailed by the system, and not visible to Global Readers (who can view TAP details without reading the code itself).

prompt: A new hire signs in with a single-use TAP, starts device enrolment, and reaches the Windows Hello for Business registration step 25 minutes later. Registration fails. What happened?

options.text: The registration must be completed within 10 minutes of sign-in with the one-time TAP, so the user needs a second single-use TAP (or a multi-use TAP) to finish registering Windows Hello
The TAP itself expired after 10 minutes and can never be used again for any purpose
The device must be hybrid-joined before Windows Hello can be registered with a TAP
The user must wait 24 hours before a second TAP can be issued

explanation: Correct: a one-time TAP requires the passwordless registration to be completed within 10 minutes of sign-in, so a slow enrolment needs a second single-use TAP (or a multi-use TAP). The 10-minute rule applies to new authentication method registrations requiring MFA, not to the TAP's own lifetime, and it is not a device or network problem.

prompt: Two guests need onboarding help: one is an internal guest with methods registered in your Entra ID, the other is an external guest. Which one can your help desk give a Temporary Access Pass?

options.text: Any guest can receive a TAP, including external guests, as long as an Authentication Administrator creates it
Only members can receive a TAP; no guest of any kind can
A TAP can be added to an internal guest, but not to an external guest — attempting it returns an error
External guests can receive a TAP only if cross-tenant access is disabled

explanation: Correct: a TAP can be added as a sign-in method to an internal guest (UserType Guest with methods registered in Entra ID), but not to other guest types — attempting to add one to an external guest returns the error that a Temporary Access Pass cannot be added to an external guest user. The distinction is the guest's account type, not the admin's role or the tenant's licence.

prompt: A help-desk lead holds the Authentication Administrator role and tries to create a Temporary Access Pass for a finance administrator. The option is unavailable. A Privileged Authentication Administrator does it in seconds. Why?

options.text: Any administrator can create a TAP for any user, including themselves
An Authentication Administrator can create a TAP for members but not for admins; a Privileged Authentication Administrator is needed for admin accounts
Only Global Administrators can create a TAP, regardless of the target user
A Global Reader can create and read TAP codes for any user

explanation: Correct: Privileged Authentication Administrators can create, delete, and view a TAP for admins and members (except themselves); Authentication Administrators can do the same for members only; Authentication Policy Administrators enable TAP and edit the policy. A Global Reader can view TAP details but not the code. The help-desk lead with only Authentication Administrator cannot create a TAP for an admin.

prompt: Your SSPR policy requires two authentication methods to reset a password. A user has registered Microsoft Authenticator push and a software OATH token, and no other method. Can they reset their password?

options.text: No — Authenticator, software OATH, and hardware OATH tokens count as a single authentication method for SSPR, so they still need a different second method
Yes — Authenticator push plus a software OATH code are two independent methods
Yes — but only if the OATH token is hardware rather than software
Yes — the two-method rule counts verification codes and push notifications separately inside the Authenticator app

explanation: Correct: for SSPR, Microsoft Authenticator, software OATH tokens, and hardware OATH tokens count as a single authentication method — a user cannot combine them to satisfy a two-method requirement. They need a genuinely different second method, such as voice call, SMS, or email OTP. The other options treat each app-based method as independent, which Learn explicitly rejects.

prompt: A federated user whose password is managed on-premises tries SSPR. The tenant has not deployed password writeback. What happens?

options.text: The user can reset in the cloud portal and the new password syncs down automatically
The user can reset using any registered method, because SSPR always writes back by default
The user must use a Temporary Access Pass instead, which bypasses writeback
The user cannot reset through SSPR and is asked to contact their administrator, because writeback is not deployed and the password is managed on-premises

explanation: Correct: if the password is managed on-premises and SSPR writeback is not deployed, the user is asked to contact their administrator — they cannot reset through the cloud portal. With writeback enabled, federated, pass-through, or password-hash-synchronised users can reset. The other options invent a cloud reset path that does not exist without writeback.

prompt: A user has lost all authentication methods. The help desk proposes Verified ID as their new MFA method going forward. What is wrong with that plan?

options.text: Verified ID can be used as a primary sign-in method in place of a password
Verified ID can satisfy an MFA challenge when the user has no phone
Verified ID is not an authentication method at all — it provides cryptographic proof of identity for account recovery, and cannot be used for sign-in, MFA, or SSPR
Verified ID is a second factor that can be combined with a password for MFA

explanation: Correct: Verified ID is an identity verification capability, not a traditional authentication method — it cannot be used for sign-in, MFA, or SSPR, and provides proof of identity for account recovery when all authentication methods are lost. The other options treat it as a sign-in or MFA method, which Learn explicitly rules out.

prompt: An architect is confused about two controls: the Authentication methods policy and Conditional Access authentication strengths. How do they relate?

options.text: The Authentication methods policy is redundant once a strength exists — delete it and use strengths alone
The Authentication methods policy scopes which methods users may register and use; the authentication strength further restricts which of those methods satisfy access to a sensitive resource
The authentication strength enables the methods, and the Authentication methods policy enforces them at sign-in
A Conditional Access policy enables the methods directly, so neither the methods policy nor the strength is needed

explanation: Correct: the Authentication methods policy scopes methods per user and group, while an authentication strength restricts methods further for specific scenarios such as sensitive resource access, user risk, and location. A Conditional Access policy cannot enable a method, and the strength does not replace the methods policy — the two are layered, with the strength applied on top of the methods policy.

prompt: A finance group has 60 members, some of whom changed roles months ago. The security team wants a recurring check that each member still needs access, with the group owner deciding. Which Microsoft Entra ID Governance capability does this, and who is the natural reviewer?

options.text: Conditional Access, with the Global Administrator as reviewer
Entitlement management, which reviews group membership automatically with no reviewer
Access reviews, with the group owner as reviewer, run on a recurring schedule
Privileged Identity Management, with the group members reviewing themselves only

explanation: Correct: access reviews automate recurring reviews of group membership, application access, and role assignments, and the group owner is a natural reviewer because they understand who needs the resource. Conditional Access enforces sign-in conditions, it does not certify ongoing need. PIM governs just-in-time activation of privileged roles, not routine group membership. Entitlement management governs access packages and can require reviews, but it does not itself certify this group without a reviewer.

prompt: During an access review of a SharePoint group, a reviewer is unsure whether a contractor still needs access and selects 'Don't know'. A second member is explicitly denied. What happens to each person?

options.text: The 'Don't know' user keeps access and the choice is recorded in audit logs; the denied user is removed when the review period ends or an administrator stops the review, not immediately
The 'Don't know' user loses access and the denied user keeps access until the next review
Both lose access immediately when the reviewer submits
Both keep access permanently because the review was inconclusive

explanation: Correct: 'Don't know' means the user keeps access and the choice is recorded in audit logs, while a denied user is not removed immediately — removal happens when the review period ends or an administrator stops the review. The other options reverse or invent the timing: denial is not instant, and 'Don't know' is not a denial.

prompt: You set up a quarterly access review for a sensitive application. You are worried reviewers will ignore the request and stale access will linger. What can you configure in advance so non-response does not silently preserve access?

options.text: Enable Conditional Access for the application; it automatically removes users who do not respond
Nothing can be configured; non-response always preserves access
Configure the advanced setting for what happens if reviewers do not respond, so unreviewed users can have an automatic decision applied at the end of the review period, including loss of access
Make the review one-time instead of recurring; one-time reviews auto-remove non-responders by default

explanation: Correct: when an access review is set up, advanced settings let the administrator decide what happens if a reviewer does not respond — an automatic decision can be applied at the end of the period, including loss of access to the group or application. There is no such default that always preserves access, Conditional Access does not remove review subjects, and one-time versus recurring does not change the non-response rule.

prompt: Your tenant has many guest users from partner organisations who were invited for projects that have now ended. You want them to re-certify their own continued need for access every quarter. What is required, and what is the mechanism?

options.text: Guest users can only be reviewed by a Global Administrator, and only with a P1 licence
Lifecycle workflows, which delete guest accounts automatically with no licence requirement
Conditional Access only; access reviews cannot review guest users and need no licence
Access reviews for guests, with guests reviewing their own access; this requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance

explanation: Correct: guest access review guidance says you can ask guests themselves (or a decision maker) to participate and re-certify their access, and the prerequisite is Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance. Conditional Access does not certify access, guests are not restricted to Global Administrator review, and lifecycle workflows are a different capability with their own Governance licensing.

prompt: A project needs a bundle for external consultants: membership of two groups, a role in one application, and access to one SharePoint site, all requested in one place with approval and an expiry date. What should you create in Microsoft Entra entitlement management?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy covering the two groups
An administrative unit, which automatically grants the bundle to anyone placed in it
A single access package in a catalog, containing the groups, application role, and SharePoint site role, with an assignment policy for request, approval, and duration
A lifecycle workflow, which bundles resources but cannot include SharePoint sites

explanation: Correct: an access package bundles group and team memberships, application roles, and SharePoint site roles into one governed request, held in a catalog, with assignment policies defining who can request it, approval, and duration. Conditional Access enforces sign-in conditions, it does not package resources. Lifecycle workflows automate joiner/mover/leaver tasks, they are not the packaging mechanism. Administrative units scope administration, they do not grant a resource bundle.

prompt: A contractor is assigned an access package for 90 days. The project ends on day 90 and nobody remembers to remove the access. What happens under entitlement management?

options.text: Only the SharePoint access is removed; group memberships granted by the package remain
The assignment expires at the end of its configured duration and Microsoft Entra removes the resource roles delivered through the package
The assignment renews automatically for another 90 days unless the user declines
Nothing; access package assignments are permanent until an administrator manually removes them

explanation: Correct: assignment policies define duration, and when an assignment expires or is removed, Microsoft Entra removes the resource roles delivered through the package — that time limit is one of the strongest entitlement controls against temporary access becoming permanent. Assignments are not permanent by default, renewal requires a renewal policy and approval where configured, and expiry removes the package-delivered roles, not just one resource type.

prompt: You want users from three partner organisations to be able to request access to your resources, but users from any other organisation must not. Where do you control which external organisations are allowed to request access?

options.text: By creating a separate tenant for each partner and federating all three
In Conditional Access named locations, by listing the partner countries
In the access review settings, which maintain the allowed-organisation list

In entitlement management, by specifying the connected organisations whose identities are allowed to request access; approved requesters are added as B2B guests and automatically removed when their access expires or is revoked

explanation: Correct: in entitlement management you specify the other organisations (connected organisations) whose identities are allowed to request access. When a request is approved they are added as a B2B guest and assigned the access, and entitlement management automatically removes the guest from the directory when their access expires or is revoked. Named locations control geography, not partner organisations. Access reviews certify existing access, they do not admit new organisations. Separate tenants are unnecessary for this.

prompt: Your finance controls say no one person may hold both the 'payment approver' access package and the 'payment requester' access package. Which entitlement management control enforces this at request time?

options.text: A separation of duties check on access requests in entitlement management
A Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for both packages
An access review, which blocks the second request while the first is active
A lifecycle workflow, which removes the first package when the second is requested

explanation: Correct: entitlement management can enforce separation of duties checks on access requests, so a request that would give one person two conflicting packages is blocked. Conditional Access adds sign-in conditions, it does not compare package combinations. Access reviews certify access after it is granted, they do not block a conflicting request. Lifecycle workflows automate joiner/mover/leaver tasks, not request-time conflict checks.

prompt: A new employee starts in 7 days. HR wants their manager to receive an email with a Temporary Access Pass before day one, and the account enabled on the start date. Which lifecycle workflow pattern fits, and what drives its timing?

options.text: A leaver workflow, triggered by employeeLeaveDateTime
A joiner workflow, with a time-based trigger measured against the employeeHireDate attribute — for example, 7 days before that date
A mover workflow, triggered when the department attribute changes
An on-demand workflow, which only runs when an administrator clicks Run for each user

explanation: Correct: joiner workflows cover the period before and at employment start, and the documented example is exactly this: send a manager an email 7 days before the value in the employeeHireDate attribute. Leaver workflows run around departure, driven by employeeLeaveDateTime. Mover workflows respond to role or department changes. On-demand execution exists, but the scheduled pre-hire pattern is time-based, not per-user manual runs.

prompt: An employee leaves the company. Which set of tasks is a leaver lifecycle workflow designed to automate?

options.text: Require the leaver to complete MFA again and issue them a new Temporary Access Pass for their next employer
Only send a farewell email; all access removal must be done manually in each application
Disable the account, remove group memberships, revoke access, remove licence assignments, and notify the manager — timed around the employee leave date
Create a new mailbox, assign a manager, and grant the leaver access to the new team's SharePoint site

explanation: Correct: leaver workflows automate removal of access when someone leaves scope: disabling the account, removing group and Teams memberships, revoking tokens and access package assignments, removing licences, and notifying stakeholders, timed before, on, or after the leave date. Creating access for a new team is a joiner/mover task. Issuing a pass for a next employer is not a leaver task. The point of the workflow is that removal is automated, not left manual in each application.

prompt: Your legal team wants every employee to accept a new acceptable-use policy, presented as a PDF, before they can access cloud apps, and to re-accept it after a set number of days. Which feature does this, and what licence is needed to configure it?

options.text: An access review, which needs no licence and presents the PDF at review time
Microsoft Entra terms of use, enforced with a Conditional Access policy, requiring Microsoft Entra ID P1 licences
A sensitivity label, which presents the PDF when a document is opened
A DLP policy, which blocks access until the user accepts the policy in the Purview portal

explanation: Correct: terms of use policies present information to users before granting access, are uploaded as a PDF, support a duration before re-acceptance is required, and are enforced with a Conditional Access policy; configuring them requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 licences. Access reviews certify access, they do not present a policy at sign-in. Sensitivity labels classify content. DLP monitors and blocks sensitive data movement, it does not collect policy acceptance.

prompt: You create an access package for external auditors. Before they receive any resource, they must accept your organisation's terms of use as part of requesting the package. Where is that acceptance enforced?

options.text: In the access package's assignment policy, which can require acceptance of terms of use before the assignment is granted
Only at sign-in, through Conditional Access — access packages cannot require terms of use
By the reviewer in the quarterly access review, who asks each auditor verbally
In the catalog settings, which apply terms of use to every package in the tenant automatically

explanation: Correct: an access package assignment policy can require the requester to accept terms of use as part of the request, so acceptance is a condition of the assignment itself. Conditional Access terms of use is a separate sign-in enforcement and is not the package mechanism. Catalog settings organise packages, they do not impose acceptance on every package. A reviewer's verbal check is not an enforced control.

prompt: An access review of a privileged group has two reviewers: the group owner and the user's manager. The owner approves a member's continued access, then the manager denies it. The member's last sign-in was 45 days ago and their access differs from their peers. What is the recorded outcome, and what does the system recommend?

options.text: The owner's approval wins because owners outrank managers, and the system recommends approval because the user signed in recently
Both responses are averaged, so the user keeps access, and the system makes no recommendation for inactive users
The manager's denial is ignored because only one reviewer may respond per user

The last submitted response is recorded, so the manager's denial is the outcome; the system recommends denial for users inactive 30 days or more and for peer outliers, and the denied user is removed when the review ends or is stopped, not immediately

explanation: Correct: if there are multiple reviewers, the last submitted response is recorded — so the later denial governs. The system recommends denial when a user has been inactive for 30 days or more, and when a user does not have the same access as their peers. Denial does not remove the user immediately; removal happens when the review period ends or an administrator stops the review. There is no owner-outranks-manager rule and no averaging.

prompt: You run an access review for guest users in a Team and its groups. You want denied guests to lose access completely — not just lose the group — and you want non-responding reviewers to cost the guest their access too. Which combination of settings achieves this?

options.text: Set 'If reviewers don't respond' to 'Take no action' and set the denied-guest action to 'Remove user from group only'
Set 'Auto apply results to resource' off and rely on the reviewer to delete each guest manually after the review
Run the review as a one-time review; guest deletion is automatic in one-time reviews with no settings needed

Set 'Auto apply results to resource' on, set 'If reviewers don't respond' to 'Remove access', and set 'Action to apply on denied guest users' to 'Block from signing in for 30 days then remove user from the tenant'

explanation: Correct: the guest review guidance gives exactly this combination for Teams and groups: auto-apply results to the resource, non-response set to Remove access, and denied guests set to block sign-in for 30 days then remove the user from the tenant — which immediately blocks sign-in and automatically deletes the B2B account after 30 days. With auto-apply off, nothing is enforced automatically. 'Take no action' preserves stale access, and one-time versus recurring does not auto-delete guests.

prompt: A company uses an automatic assignment policy in entitlement management: anyone whose department attribute is 'Finance' is automatically assigned the Finance access package. An employee moves from Finance to Operations, and HR updates the department attribute the same day. What should happen to the Finance package, and what is the trap if the move is only recorded in a spreadsheet?

options.text: The employee keeps the Finance package until the next quarterly access review, because automatic policies never react to attribute changes

The Finance package assignment is automatically removed because automatic assignment policies add and remove group memberships, application roles, and SharePoint roles based on changes to user attributes — but only if the attribute change actually reaches Microsoft Entra; a spreadsheet-only move leaves the stale access in place
The package is removed only if a lifecycle workflow also runs; entitlement management alone cannot remove access
The Finance package stays because automatic policies only add access, never remove it; the spreadsheet is the authoritative record

explanation: Correct: automatic assignment policies add and remove a user's group memberships, application roles, and SharePoint site roles based on changes to their attributes — so a real department change removes the Finance package. The trap is the data source: if HR only updates a spreadsheet, the attribute in Entra never changes and the policy never fires. Automatic policies do remove access, they do not wait for a review, and no separate lifecycle workflow is required for the removal.

prompt: An access package for contractors has a 60-day assignment, requires manager approval, and requires a quarterly access review of the package assignments. A contractor's assignment reaches day 60 while the quarterly review is still two weeks away, and the manager wants the access to continue. What happens, and what is the correct way to continue it?

options.text: The assignment continues until the quarterly review decides, because the review overrides the expiry
The manager can extend it by approving the access review early; the review itself renews the assignment
The assignment renews automatically for 60 days because a review is pending

The assignment expires at day 60 and the package-delivered access is removed; continuing it requires renewal under the assignment policy (with approval where configured), not waiting for the access review

explanation: Correct: duration and review are separate controls. Expiry at day 60 removes the resource roles delivered through the package, regardless of a pending review — the review certifies ongoing need, it does not extend an expired assignment. Continuation is through renewal under the assignment policy, with approval where the policy requires it. There is no automatic renewal merely because a review is pending, and approving a review does not renew an assignment.

prompt: You build a joiner workflow that sends a welcome email 3 days before employeeHireDate and enables the account on the start date. In testing, half the new hires never receive the email and their accounts are not enabled on time. HR confirms the hires exist in the HR system but their hire dates were entered a week late. What is the root cause?

options.text: The workflow's time-based trigger is measured against the employeeHireDate attribute in Microsoft Entra, so if that attribute is missing or late, the trigger fires late or not at all — the workflow is only as accurate as the attribute data feeding it
The hires were in the wrong administrative unit, and lifecycle workflows ignore administrative units entirely
Lifecycle workflows only run on-demand, so scheduled triggers never fire without an administrator clicking Run
The workflow failed because joiner workflows cannot send email; only leaver workflows can

explanation: Correct: a time-based trigger schedules against user attributes such as employeeHireDate, so late or missing attribute data means the trigger fires late or misses the window — automation depends on accurate, populated attributes, typically fed by HR-driven provisioning. Scheduled triggers do fire automatically; joiner workflows can send email (the pre-hire Temporary Access Pass email is the documented example). Administrative unit scope is a separate scoping issue, not the cause described here.

prompt: Your tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P1 for every user. You try to create lifecycle workflows for joiner and leaver automation. What happens, and what licence is actually required?

options.text: It works for leaver workflows only; joiner workflows need P2
It is blocked — using lifecycle workflows requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite licences, on top of P1/P2 for users in scope; P1 alone does not include it
It works — P1 includes lifecycle workflows for all users
It works, but only for 100 users; beyond that you need P2

explanation: Correct: using lifecycle workflows requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite licences. P1 alone does not include the feature, and the distinction is not joiner versus leaver, nor a 100-user threshold — 100 is the limit on the number of workflows you can create, not a licensing threshold.

prompt: You enforce terms of use with a Conditional Access policy targeting All users and All cloud apps, and you turn on 'Require users to consent on every device'. Two days later, enrolment of new devices through Intune fails and your break-glass accounts cannot sign in. What went wrong?

options.text: The policy failed because terms of use require P2, not P1
Terms of use cannot target All users; the policy should have targeted only guests
Per-device consent only applies to Windows devices, so Intune enrolment on other platforms should have worked

You failed to exclude the emergency-access accounts and the Intune Enrollment app from the policy — break-glass accounts must be excluded from every Conditional Access policy, and the Intune Enrollment app is not supported for per-device terms of use and must be excluded; service accounts are also not supported for terms of use enforcement

explanation: Correct: break-glass accounts must be excluded from every Conditional Access policy or a misconfiguration can lock you out, and the Intune Enrollment app is not supported for per-device terms of use and must be excluded; Conditional Access terms of use controls also do not support enforcement on service accounts, which must be excluded. Terms of use require P1, not P2, and per-device consent is not Windows-only.

prompt: An administrator creates a terms of use document in the Entra admin centre, uploads the PDF, and sets a re-acceptance period — but creates no Conditional Access policy and selects no enforcement template. Users sign in the next day and are never shown the terms. Why?

options.text: Terms of use are only a document definition until enforced — they are presented only when a Conditional Access policy enforces them as a grant control, so creating the document alone changes nothing at sign-in
The PDF was the wrong file type; terms of use require a Word document
The re-acceptance period had not yet expired, so nobody was asked
Terms of use only apply to guest users, so members were correctly not shown them

explanation: Correct: a terms of use policy is enforced with a Conditional Access policy (via a template or a custom policy with the terms of use grant control). Without that enforcement, the document exists but is never presented at sign-in. The upload format is PDF, the re-acceptance period governs repeat prompts after acceptance, and terms of use apply to members as well as guests depending on the policy scope.

prompt: A review finds a service account with broad unused permissions across Azure, AWS, and GCP, and an administrator with standing Owner on three subscriptions. Your predecessor's notes say 'use Microsoft Entra Permissions Management to discover the unused permissions across all three clouds.' What is the current status of that tool?

options.text: Permissions Management is still available and is the right tool for this discovery
Access reviews are the replacement — they scan AWS and GCP permissions directly
Defender for Cloud secure score removes the unused permissions automatically when the score drops

Permissions Management was the multicloud CIEM tool for this discovery, but Microsoft retired and discontinued it on November 1, 2025, so it can no longer be deployed — PIM alone does not discover unused cloud permissions

explanation: Correct: Microsoft Entra Permissions Management was the multicloud CIEM solution that discovered granted-versus-used permissions across Azure, AWS, and GCP and right-sized them — exactly the discovery this review needs. But Microsoft stopped selling it on April 1, 2025 and retired and discontinued support on November 1, 2025, so it can no longer be deployed for this discovery. Access reviews do not scan AWS and GCP permissions, Defender for Cloud secure score does not remove permissions, and Conditional Access does not discover unused permissions. PIM governs just-in-time activation of privileged roles; it does not discover unused cloud permissions either.

prompt: A department wants to manage its own access packages for its SharePoint sites without involving central IT for every change. How does entitlement management delegate this?

options.text: Only Global Administrators can create access packages; delegation is not possible
Access packages live in catalogs, and catalog owners can delegate to access package managers who define policies for request, approval, and expiry
Any user can create an access package in any catalog without owning the resources
Catalogs are only labels; all access packages are created by Microsoft support

explanation: Correct: access packages live in catalogs, and a catalog owner can add other identities as catalog co-owners or access package managers — delegation lets non-administrators create access packages from resources they own, while an administrator can add resources to any catalog. The other options either centralise everything with IT or invent a tenant-wide delegation that does not exist.

prompt: One access package must serve both employees and partner users, but with different approval rules and durations for each group. How do you model this in entitlement management?

options.text: One policy that treats employees and external identities identically
Two access packages that cannot share resources
One access package with two policies: one for employees to request access and a second for external identities to request access
One catalog per population, with no shared access package allowed

explanation: Correct: an access package can have two policies — one for employees to request access and a second for external identities to request access — each with its own rules for who can request, approval, and duration. A single policy cannot express two different populations cleanly, and the two populations are not merged into one guest pool.

prompt: A project team mixes employees and external consultants who need the same groups, apps, and SharePoint sites. Can one entitlement management setup govern both populations?

options.text: Entitlement management only governs internal employees; external users need a separate system
Entitlement management governs groups, applications, and SharePoint sites for internal identities and for identities from outside the organisation
Entitlement management only governs SharePoint sites, not groups or applications
Entitlement management only governs external users; internal access must use another tool

explanation: Correct: entitlement management can govern access for internal identities and for identities originating outside the organisation — including groups, applications, and SharePoint sites — and approved external requesters are invited as B2B guests. It is not internal-only, not guest-only, and not limited to SharePoint.

prompt: An access package contains three groups and an application. What does its assignment policy control?

options.text: A policy defines which sign-in methods users must use
A policy defines the resources in the package
A policy defines who can request access, who approves it, and how long the assignment lasts before it expires
A policy defines the catalog the package belongs to

explanation: Correct: a policy defines the rules for assignment — which identities can request, the approval process, and the duration before the assignment expires — and access is time-limited so it expires if not renewed. A policy does not set sign-in conditions (that is Conditional Access) and does not define the resources themselves (those are the package contents).

prompt: Your tenant has Entra ID P1 only. You try to create your first access package. What happens?

options.text: It is blocked — entitlement management requires Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite subscriptions
It works — P1 includes entitlement management for all users
It works — P2 includes entitlement management, so P1 users are covered
It works for the first 30 days on any licence, then stops

explanation: Correct: entitlement management requires Entra ID Governance or Entra Suite subscriptions for your organisation's users. P1 alone does not include it, and a P2 licence does not substitute — the feature is a Governance capability. Free licences do not include it either.

prompt: You need to review three things: membership of a security group, assignments of an access package, and holders of the Global Administrator role. Where is each review created?

options.text: All reviews are created in Conditional Access
All reviews are created in PIM, regardless of what is reviewed
Where you create a review depends on what you review: Entra roles in PIM, access package assignments in entitlement management, groups or apps in access reviews
All reviews are created in lifecycle workflows

explanation: Correct: reviews can be created in access reviews, enterprise apps, PIM, or entitlement management depending on what is reviewed — Entra roles are reviewed in PIM, access package assignments in entitlement management, and groups or apps in access reviews. There is no single creation point for every review type, and reviews are not created in Conditional Access.

prompt: A group gives guests access to business-sensitive content. Employee access in the tenant is automated with lifecycle workflows. Who is responsible for confirming the guests still need access?

options.text: The guest's manager in their home organisation
The Global Administrator, for every group
The group owner, who must confirm the guests still have a legitimate business need for access
Nobody — guest access in groups is never reviewed

explanation: Correct: group owners are responsible for confirming that guests in their groups still have a legitimate business need — employee access may be automated by lifecycle workflows, but invited guests are not covered by that automation. The guest's manager, the Global Administrator, and the guest themselves are not the designated reviewer for group guest access.

prompt: Your HR data is not in Entra ID, so dynamic group rules cannot capture who should keep access to a legacy SharePoint site. Which governance capability handles this, and why?

options.text: When automation is not possible, when a group takes on a new purpose, for business-critical data access, and to maintain a policy exception list with regular review
Only when a group has more than 100 members
Only for privileged roles, never for groups or applications
Only when Conditional Access is unavailable

explanation: Correct: access reviews are the tool for the hard cases — when automation is not possible, when a group is used for a new purpose, for business-critical data access, and to maintain a policy exception list with audit proof. They are not a replacement for Conditional Access, not a PIM substitute, and not limited to privileged roles.

prompt: Your HR team wants one governance capability covering a new hire, an employee changing departments, and an employee retiring. Which lifecycle phases do lifecycle workflows cover?

options.text: Joiner and Leaver only
Joiner, Mover, and Leaver
Joiner, Mover, Leaver, and Suspended
Onboarding, Offboarding, and Auditing only

explanation: Correct: lifecycle workflows manage the three phases — Joiner (entering scope), Mover (moving between boundaries, needing more or different access), and Leaver (leaving scope, needing access removed). A fourth 'suspended' phase does not exist in the model, and the phases are not joiner/leaver only.

prompt: An architect asks what a lifecycle workflow is made of. Which description is correct?

options.text: A workflow is a single task that runs once for one user
A workflow is a static group that never changes
A workflow consists of tasks that run automatically when triggered, plus execution conditions defining who is in scope and when it runs
A workflow is a manual checklist an administrator follows for each hire

explanation: Correct: workflows consist of tasks and execution conditions — a task is a specific action that runs automatically when triggered, and the execution condition defines the scope of who is affected and when the workflow runs. A workflow is not a single task, not a static group, and not a manual checklist.

prompt: An employee moves from Marketing to Sales. They need the Sales groups and apps, and should lose the Marketing-only access. Which lifecycle workflow pattern fits?

options.text: A mover workflow, triggered by the move between organisational boundaries
A joiner workflow, because the user is joining a new team
A leaver workflow, because the user is leaving the old team
An on-demand workflow, because department changes cannot trigger workflows

explanation: Correct: a mover workflow fits a department change — the user moves between boundaries and may need more or different access. A joiner workflow is for entering scope, a leaver for leaving scope, and on-demand execution is for manual runs, not for an attribute-driven move.

prompt: Your team is designing a large lifecycle automation programme with separate workflows for every department and scenario. What is the workflow limit?

options.text: There is no limit on the number of workflows
You can create up to 100 workflows in total
You can create up to 100 workflows per user
You can create up to 1,000 workflows, but only 100 can be active

explanation: Correct: you can create, manage, and delete workflows up to a total limit of 100 workflows, and up to 100 custom task extensions. The limit is on workflows, not users, not tasks per workflow, and not executions per day.

prompt: A joiner workflow needs to call an internal HR API that no built-in lifecycle task supports. How do you extend the workflow?

options.text: You cannot extend a lifecycle workflow — only the built-in tasks are available
You must replace the workflow with a standalone Logic App and abandon lifecycle workflows
You can integrate Logic Apps tasks to extend the workflow for more complex scenarios through your existing Logic Apps
You can only extend the workflow with email tasks

explanation: Correct: lifecycle workflows can integrate with Logic Apps tasks to extend workflows for complex scenarios through existing Logic Apps — the extension point for anything the built-in tasks cannot do. It is not a PowerShell-only path, not a replacement of the workflow, and not limited to email tasks.

prompt: A joiner workflow should automatically give every new Finance hire the Finance access package on day one, and remove it when they leave Finance. Can a lifecycle workflow do that?

options.text: Yes — lifecycle workflows can be used to automate assigning and removing access packages for users
No — access packages can only be assigned by users requesting them
No — access packages can only be assigned by administrators manually
Yes, but only for leaver workflows, not joiner or mover workflows

explanation: Correct: lifecycle workflows can automate assigning and removing access packages for users — the joiner/mover/leaver automation can drive package assignment as part of the lifecycle. It is not limited to email, not limited to leavers, and does not require a separate entitlement product.

prompt: HR wants new hires added to their department's static security group three days before their start date, without writing one rule per group. Dynamic group rules cannot express the date trigger. Which approach fits?

options.text: Dynamic group memberships, because they need one rule per group
Lifecycle workflows, because they manage static groups without one rule per group, scope by user attributes including dates, and can act on the group itself
Neither — group membership for new hires must always be manual
Administrative units, because they replace both features

explanation: Correct: lifecycle workflows manage static groups, where no dynamic rule is needed, and the workflow rules determine which users are in scope — not which group — so one workflow can manage membership across groups. Dynamic groups need one rule per group and only support attributes they understand; lifecycle workflows also act on the group, not just membership, and can trigger on dates such as days before employeeHireDate.

prompt: Legal wants 45 separate terms of use documents, one per department policy. What is the tenant limit?

options.text: There is no limit on the number of terms per tenant
The limit is 40 terms per user, with no tenant limit
You can add no more than 40 terms per tenant
The limit is 10 terms per tenant

explanation: Correct: a tenant can have no more than 40 terms. The limit is per tenant, not per user or per policy, and it is not unlimited — a 45-term plan must be consolidated.

prompt: A terms of use policy expires consents every 30 days. A user accepted 29 days ago and has an active session on day 31. When are they prompted to reaccept?

options.text: Users are prompted to reaccept only if their session expired; an expired consent alone does not interrupt an active session
Users are signed out immediately the moment consent expires, even mid-session
Users are never prompted again once they have accepted once, even after expiry
Users are prompted at the next sign-in regardless of whether the session expired

explanation: Correct: users whose consent expires are prompted to reaccept the terms only if their session expired — an expired consent alone does not interrupt an active session. The other options assume an immediate prompt regardless of session state, or that re-acceptance never happens.

prompt: Legal updates the acceptable-use PDF with a new clause and wants every employee to accept the new version. What must the administrator do when uploading it?

options.text: The new version applies to everyone immediately, with no setting needed
Previous consent is automatically voided for everyone as soon as any new version is uploaded
You must delete and recreate the terms of use policy to force reacceptance
Use the Require reaccept toggle when updating the version, so users are prompted to accept the new version at next sign-in

explanation: Correct: when a new version of the terms is uploaded, the Require reaccept toggle makes users accept the new version next time they sign in — without it, previous consent stays current and only new users or users whose consent expires see the new version. Deleting and recreating is not required, and the new version does not apply instantly to everyone.

prompt: You enable 'Require users to consent on every device' for terms of use. New device enrolment through Intune starts failing. What is the cause?

options.text: The Intune Enrollment app is fully supported for per-device terms of use
Per-device terms of use work for B2B users without restriction
The Intune Enrollment app is not supported for per-device terms of use and must be excluded from the policy
Per-device terms of use require the user to reinstall the Intune app first

explanation: Correct: the Intune Enrollment app is not supported for per-device terms of use and must be excluded from any Conditional Access policy requiring terms of use — otherwise enrolment breaks. B2B users are also not supported for per-device terms. The other options invent support that does not exist.

prompt: Your tenant's P1 licences lapse during a renewal gap. What happens to the stored record of who accepted the terms of use?

options.text: Acceptance records are deleted when the terms of use are deleted, when the tenant loses its P1 or P2 licences, or when the tenant is deleted
Acceptance records are never deleted, even if the tenant is deleted
Acceptance records are deleted automatically 30 days after each acceptance
Acceptance records are deleted when a user changes department

explanation: Correct: user acceptance records are deleted when an admin deletes the terms of use, when the tenant loses its P1 or P2 licences, or when the tenant is deleted. They are not deleted on a schedule, not kept forever, and not deleted when a user changes department.

prompt: A governance report cites a rising Permission Creep Index (PCI) for the tenant. What does PCI measure?

options.text: The number of users in the tenant with any admin role
An aggregated metric that periodically evaluates the level of risk associated with unused or excessive permissions across identities and resources
The percentage of sign-ins that use MFA
The number of days since the last access review

explanation: Correct: the Permission Creep Index is an aggregated metric that periodically evaluates the risk associated with the number of unused or excessive permissions across identities and resources — it measures how much damage identities can cause based on the permissions they have. It is not a count of users, not a compliance score, and not a measure of sign-in frequency.

prompt: A team adopting Permissions Management wants to start by auto-deleting unused permissions on day one. What order does Microsoft recommend for its three use cases, and why?

options.text: Monitor, remediate, discover
Remediate, discover, monitor
Discover and monitor at the same time, then remediate
Discover, remediate, then monitor — in that order

explanation: Correct: Permissions Management was designed to be stepped through in order — discover, then remediate, then monitor — because you cannot act on what has not been discovered, and cannot continually evaluate what has not been remediated. The other orders invert the logic.

prompt: Before its retirement, what did Microsoft Entra Permissions Management actually do?

options.text: It managed on-premises Active Directory group membership
It issued certificates for service principals
It detected, automatically right-sized, and continuously monitored unused and excessive permissions across Azure, AWS, and GCP
It replaced Conditional Access for multicloud sign-ins

explanation: Correct: Permissions Management detected, automatically right-sized, and continuously monitored unused and excessive permissions across Azure, AWS, and GCP — the multicloud CIEM capability. It did not manage on-premises AD, did not issue certificates, and did not replace Conditional Access.

prompt: A user is given the User Administrator role as an eligible assignment. A colleague insists the user can reset passwords immediately. What must happen before they can use it?

options.text: Nothing — eligible means the role is already active
They must activate it (for example, complete MFA, give a justification, and get approval if required), and the activation lasts only for a limited time
A Global Administrator must delete the assignment and re-create it as active
They must wait 24 hours; eligible assignments activate automatically overnight

explanation: Correct: eligible means 'you may activate it when you need it.' Activation can require MFA, a justification, and approval, and it lasts for a preconfigured period before it expires. Active means standing privilege with no activation step. The first option describes active, not eligible. The other two are not how PIM works.

prompt: You configure PIM for the User Administrator role. An auditor asks which controls you can require when someone activates it. Which settings are available?

options.text: Only a justification — MFA and approval cannot be required for Entra roles
Maximum activation duration (for example, 8 hours), MFA on activation, justification, and approval by a designated approver
Only approval — duration is always permanent once approved
None — PIM settings apply only to Azure roles, not Entra roles

explanation: Correct: PIM role settings let you set maximum activation duration, require MFA on activation, require justification, and require approval by designated approvers, plus notifications. The other options each drop most of those controls or limit PIM to Azure roles only — PIM covers both Entra roles and Azure resources.

prompt: You need a service principal used by an automation runbook to have Global Administrator rights for a weekend migration. What can PIM do here?

options.text: Make the service principal eligible for Global Administrator, so it can activate the role when the runbook starts
Give the service principal a time-limited active assignment only — service principals cannot be eligible for Entra roles, Azure roles, or PIM for Groups
Make the service principal eligible, but only if it is in a role-assignable group
Nothing — service principals cannot hold Entra roles at all

explanation: Correct: service principals cannot be eligible — only time-limited active assignments are allowed for them, for Entra roles, Azure roles, and PIM for Groups. The first and third options assume eligibility works for service principals. The fourth is too strong — service principals can hold roles via active assignments.

prompt: You set the User Administrator role to require approval, MFA, justification, and a maximum activation duration of 4 hours. A colleague is eligible for Global Administrator. What applies to them?

options.text: The same settings — PIM settings are tenant-wide and apply to all roles
Nothing yet — role settings are per role, so Global Administrator has its own settings until you configure them
The same settings, but the maximum duration is always 8 hours for Global Administrator regardless
Global Administrator cannot use PIM at all — it must be permanently active

explanation: Correct: PIM role settings are per role. Configuring User Administrator does not configure Global Administrator — each role has its own settings for maximum duration, MFA, justification, and approval. The first option assumes tenant-wide settings. The third invents a fixed 8-hour rule for Global Administrator. The fourth is false — Global Administrator is a PIM-manageable Entra role.

prompt: You want just-in-time membership of a security group that grants access to Intune and Key Vault. The group is dynamic (membership rule-based) and synced from on-premises. Can you enable PIM for Groups on it?

options.text: Yes — any security group can be enabled for PIM for Groups
No — dynamic groups and on-premises synced groups cannot be enabled for PIM for Groups
Yes, but only for the owner role, not the member role
Yes, if you first make the group role-assignable — that fixes both problems

explanation: Correct: dynamic groups and on-premises synced groups cannot be enabled for PIM for Groups. Making a group role-assignable does not fix dynamic or synced status. The first option ignores the restriction. The third invents a member/owner split for this restriction — both are blocked.

prompt: A Global Administrator is on holiday. An admin needs User Administrator for 2 hours to reset a contractor's password. The admin is eligible for User Administrator in PIM, with role settings: maximum duration 8 hours, require MFA, require justification, require approval by the Privileged Role Administrator. The admin activates the role, provides a justification, completes MFA, and the approver approves. The admin then tries to assign an Azure Reader role on a subscription to the contractor. What happens?

options.text: It works — User Administrator in Entra includes Azure RBAC assignment rights

It fails — User Administrator is an Entra role for managing Entra resources; assigning Azure roles needs an Azure role such as Owner or Role Based Access Control Administrator on that subscription scope, which PIM for Entra does not grant
It works, but only for 2 hours — after that the Azure assignment is revoked automatically
It fails because PIM activation lasts only 8 hours, and the admin asked for 2 hours

explanation: Correct: User Administrator is an Entra role — it manages Entra resources (users, groups). It does not grant Azure Resource Manager permissions. Assigning an Azure role on a subscription needs an Azure role at that scope, such as Owner or Role Based Access Control Administrator. PIM for Entra does not grant that. The first option conflates the two RBAC systems. The third invents automatic revocation of the Azure assignment when PIM expires — the Azure assignment is separate. The fourth misreads the duration — 2 hours is within the 8-hour maximum, so duration is not the blocker.

prompt: A security group grants access to a sensitive SharePoint site. You want members to hold that membership only when they need it, activating it just-in-time with approval, instead of holding it permanently. What must be true of the group before you can use PIM for Groups on it?

options.text: The group must be role-assignable, and membership (and ownership) can then be made eligible for just-in-time activation
The group must be synced from on-premises; cloud-only groups cannot use PIM for Groups
Nothing — any group works, and PIM for Groups converts it automatically
The group must be dynamic; only dynamic groups support PIM for Groups

explanation: Correct: PIM for Groups requires a role-assignable group; once enabled, member and owner assignments can be eligible and activated just-in-time with the usual PIM controls (duration, justification, approval). Dynamic groups and on-premises synced groups cannot be enabled for PIM for Groups, so those options are backwards. Not every group qualifies — the role-assignable property is the gate.

prompt: Your tenant has 40 users permanently assigned Global Administrator. The security team wants Privileged Identity Management to surface this as a problem. Which PIM capability highlights risky privileged-role configuration?

options.text: The Entra audit log, which deletes excessive assignments after 30 days
PIM alerts, which flag issues such as excessive privileged role assignments and roles assigned to users who do not need them
Conditional Access report-only mode, which lists Global Administrators
Access reviews, which automatically convert permanent assignments to eligible ones

explanation: Correct: PIM includes alerts that flag risky configurations, including too many users assigned to a privileged role and assignments that should be eligible rather than permanent. Conditional Access report-only shows policy impact, not role hygiene. Access reviews certify access, they do not convert assignments. The audit log records events, it does not delete assignments.

prompt: A PIM role setting has 'Maximum activation duration: 8 hours' for Global Administrator, and a separate setting 'Expire eligible assignments after 90 days'. An eligible Global Administrator has not activated the role for 100 days, then activates it for a task. What happens?

options.text: The activation lasts 90 days, because the expiry setting overrides the maximum duration
They can activate for 8 hours, because the 90-day expiry only applies to active assignments, not eligible ones
They cannot activate, because the 8-hour maximum has expired; the assignment is gone
They cannot activate: the 90-day expiry removed the eligibility after 100 days without activation, so the assignment must be renewed first — the 8-hour maximum only caps how long one activation lasts

explanation: Correct: these are two different settings that sound alike. Maximum activation duration caps a single activation session. 'Expire eligible assignments' removes the eligible assignment itself if it is not used within the configured period — so after 100 days without activation, the eligibility is gone and the user cannot activate until reassigned. The 8-hour cap does not delete eligibility, and the 90-day expiry does not extend an activation to 90 days, and it applies to eligible assignments, not only active ones.

prompt: Two administrators hold the Security Administrator role: one as a permanent active assignment, one as a permanent eligible assignment. An auditor asks whether the eligible admin is less powerful. What is the correct answer?

options.text: They have identical permissions — eligible only adds an activation step, so the risk is the standing access, not a difference in power
The eligible admin has read-only permissions until activation, then full permissions
The active admin has fewer permissions because PIM restricts standing assignments
The eligible admin cannot be audited, while the active admin's actions are logged

explanation: Correct: eligible and active assignments grant exactly the same access — the only difference is that an eligible user must activate (and may need MFA, justification, or approval) while an active user holds the privilege continuously. The audit finding is the standing access itself, not a difference in power. The other options invent a permission gap that does not exist.

prompt: A departing administrator is the last active Global Administrator in the tenant. Another admin tries to remove their assignment in PIM. What happens?

options.text: PIM automatically promotes the next eligible administrator to active Global Administrator
PIM deletes the tenant after 30 days if no administrator remains
PIM prevents removal of the last active Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator role assignments
PIM allows the removal but requires a Microsoft support ticket first

explanation: Correct: PIM prevents removal of the last active Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator assignments — that guardrail exists precisely so the tenant cannot be left with no administrator. The other options describe actions PIM does not take: it does not auto-promote, does not delete the tenant, and does not require a support ticket to block the removal.

prompt: A Security Administrator wants to make a colleague eligible for the Exchange Administrator role in PIM. Can they do it?

options.text: Any Security Administrator can manage PIM assignments for other administrators
A User Administrator can manage PIM assignments for other administrators
A Security Reader can manage PIM assignments for other administrators
Only a Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator can manage assignments for other administrators

explanation: Correct: for Entra roles in PIM, only a Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator can manage assignments for other administrators. Security Administrators and Security Readers can view assignments, but cannot manage them. A User Administrator cannot manage PIM assignments for other admins.

prompt: A Privileged Role Administrator opens PIM for Azure resources and cannot see the subscription's role assignments. A colleague says their Entra role should be enough. Who is right?

options.text: Only a subscription administrator, a resource Owner, or a resource User Access Administrator can manage assignments for Azure resource roles in PIM
A Privileged Role Administrator can manage Azure resource role assignments in PIM by default
A Security Reader can manage Azure resource role assignments in PIM by default
Any Global Administrator can manage Azure resource role assignments in PIM by default

explanation: Correct: for Azure resource roles in PIM, only a subscription administrator, a resource Owner, or a resource User Access Administrator can manage assignments. Privileged Role Administrators, Security Administrators, and Security Readers do not by default have access to view or manage Azure resource role assignments in PIM — the Entra role does not cross over to Azure resources.

prompt: A consultant's time-bound eligible assignment for the Intune Administrator role expires next week, mid-project. What is the correct way to keep their access, and who must approve it?

options.text: The assignment extends itself automatically for the same duration
The user renews it themselves with no approval needed
The user requests an extension before expiry or a renewal after expiry, and either request requires approval from a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator
The assignment converts to a permanent active assignment so the work is not interrupted

explanation: Correct: when a role assignment nears expiration, the user can request an extension; when it has expired, they request a renewal — and both user-initiated actions require approval from a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator. Extensions are not automatic, renewals are not self-approved, and the assignment does not silently convert to permanent.

prompt: An eligible administrator activates the Global Administrator role, which requires approval. What happens between the activation request and the approver's decision?

options.text: The member is notified the request is pending approval and can use the role only after it is approved
The member can use the role immediately while the approval is pending
The approval is granted automatically after one hour if no approver responds
The member approves their own request by confirming the justification a second time

explanation: Correct: when approval is required, a notification appears telling the user the request is pending approval, and the member can start using the role only after the request is approved. Approval is not instant, not automatic, and not granted by the requester.

prompt: You configure PIM approval for the Security Administrator role and select a business manager with no admin roles as the approver. The manager asks whether they need an admin role to approve. What is the correct answer?

options.text: The approver must hold the same role they are approving
The approver must be a Global Administrator
The approver is chosen automatically from the tenant's Privileged Role Administrators
The approver needs no role at all and need not be an administrator; Microsoft recommends at least two approvers and there are no default approvers

explanation: Correct: the approver does not require any roles and does not need to be an administrator — approval is a designated workflow step, not a privilege. Microsoft recommends selecting at least two approvers and there are no default approvers. The other options confuse approval with role assignment.

prompt: Your two emergency-access accounts are currently eligible for Global Administrator in PIM. The CISO says this is wrong. What should the assignment be?

options.text: Make the assignment eligible with approval required, so use is audited
Make the assignment eligible with a 90-day expiry, so it is reviewed regularly
Make the Global Administrator assignment active permanent in PIM, not eligible
Make the assignment time-bound active for 8 hours each quarter

explanation: Correct: break-glass accounts must have their Global Administrator assignment as permanent active in PIM, not eligible — an eligible break-glass account could be unusable in the exact emergency it exists for. The other options all make the emergency account depend on activation, approval, or expiry.

prompt: A security group grants access to a production Key Vault. You enable PIM for Groups on it and make the members eligible. What changes for a member who needs access on Tuesday?

options.text: A member activates the group membership just-in-time for a limited period, instead of holding it permanently
The group is converted to a dynamic group with a membership rule
The group is deleted and its members are reassigned individually
Ownership is made permanent and membership is made eligible, but activation is automatic

explanation: Correct: PIM for Groups makes group membership and ownership eligible for just-in-time activation — a member activates the membership for a limited time instead of holding it permanently. It does not convert the group to dynamic, does not remove the group, and does not require the group to be deleted and recreated.

prompt: A group synced from on-premises Active Directory grants access to a sensitive SharePoint site. You try to enable PIM for Groups on it and the option is unavailable. What is the correct fix?

options.text: Enable PIM for Groups on the synced group directly — sync source does not matter
Make the synced group role-assignable and PIM for Groups will work
Convert the synced group to dynamic and enable PIM for Groups on it
Create a cloud-only role-assignable group for the just-in-time membership, because on-premises synced groups cannot be enabled for PIM for Groups

explanation: Correct: the group must be cloud-only and role-assignable — on-premises synced groups cannot be enabled for PIM for Groups, and making it role-assignable does not fix the sync source. The fix is a new cloud-only role-assignable group (or moving the membership to one), not a setting change on the synced group.

prompt: An administrator activates a role that requires approval at 2 a.m. How does the designated approver learn about the pending request?

options.text: The approver must check the PIM portal every hour; PIM sends no notifications
Notifications are sent by SMS only, so the approver needs a registered phone
PIM sends email notifications to participants and approvers, with links to activate, approve, or deny the request
The requester is notified but the approver is not — approvers must poll the audit log

explanation: Correct: PIM keeps you informed by sending email notifications to you and other participants, including links to tasks such as activating, approving, or denying a request, and delegated approvers receive email notifications when a role request is pending. There is no requirement to watch a portal, no SMS-only channel, and no silent activation.

prompt: A role's maximum activation duration is 8 hours. An eligible administrator needs the role for 2 hours. What do they do at activation time?

options.text: The user selects an activation duration within the configured maximum and provides the reason for the request
The user always receives the maximum duration, with no choice
The approver chooses the duration after approving, and the user cannot select it
The activation lasts until the user signs out, regardless of the configured maximum

explanation: Correct: an eligible user activates by selecting a specific activation duration within the maximum configured by administrators, and giving the reason for the request. The duration is chosen by the user up to the configured maximum — it is not fixed at the maximum, not chosen by the approver, and not unlimited.

prompt: A contractor needs Contributor on one resource group for a two-week migration, with approval each time they activate it. What is the correct PIM approach?

options.text: Give them Contributor permanently as an active assignment on the subscription
Give them Contributor permanently, but only at the resource-group scope
Give them the Entra User Administrator role, which includes Azure Contributor rights
Make Contributor an eligible assignment at the resource-group scope, with activation requiring justification and approval

explanation: Correct: PIM for Azure resources uses the same eligible/active model — make the role eligible at the resource-group scope with justification and approval, and the user activates it just-in-time. A permanent active assignment defeats PIM. A tenant-wide assignment is the wrong scope. And an Entra role cannot grant Azure permissions.

prompt: An auditor needs the Security Reader role only during the six-week audit window, and only when they choose to activate it. Which assignment type fits?

options.text: A time-bound eligible assignment — the member can only activate within the start and end dates
A permanent eligible assignment — the member can activate at any time forever
A time-bound active assignment — the member holds the role continuously during the window with no activation step
A permanent active assignment with a calendar reminder to remove it

explanation: Correct: a time-bound eligible assignment lets the member activate only within the start and end dates; outside that window there is nothing to activate. A permanent eligible assignment has no end date, a time-bound active assignment grants standing access during the window, and eligibility does not auto-extend.

prompt: A compliance officer asks what PIM actually delivers beyond 'eligible instead of active'. Which list is correct?

options.text: It automatically deletes any assignment older than 90 days
It replaces Conditional Access for privileged users
It provides just-in-time privileged access, time-bound assignments, approval and MFA on activation, justification, notifications, access reviews, and a downloadable audit history
It grants P2 licences to every user who activates a role

explanation: Correct: PIM provides just-in-time privileged access, time-bound access, approval, MFA on activation, justification, notifications, access reviews, and downloadable audit history. It does not delete assignments automatically, does not replace Conditional Access, and does not grant licences.

prompt: When a Privileged Role Administrator assigns an Entra role in PIM, what does the assignment itself contain?

options.text: The assignment has no scope — every PIM role applies tenant-wide
The scope is chosen by the member at activation time
The scope is the approval workflow selected for the role
The assignment includes the members, the scope limiting the role to a particular set of resources, the type, and the duration

explanation: Correct: the assignment includes the members, the scope limiting the role to a particular set of resources, the type (eligible or active), and the duration. Scope is a first-class part of the assignment — it is not tenant-wide by default, not chosen by the member, and not the same as the approval workflow.

prompt: A director asks why the organisation should bother with PIM at all, when the current admins 'have always had permanent access and nothing bad happened'. What is PIM's stated purpose?

options.text: To minimise the number of people with standing access to secure resources, reducing the chance of a malicious actor getting access or an authorised user inadvertently impacting a sensitive resource
To reduce the number of administrators the organisation employs
To eliminate the need for Conditional Access policies for privileged users
To make all administrative access permanent so audits are simpler

explanation: Correct: PIM's purpose is to minimise the number of people with access to secure resources, because that reduces the chance of a malicious actor getting access and of an authorised user inadvertently impacting a sensitive resource — while still letting users carry out privileged operations just-in-time. It is not about headcount reduction, cost, or removing the need for admins.

prompt: Your team is scoping a PIM rollout. Which three things can PIM actually manage?

options.text: Microsoft Entra roles and SharePoint site permissions only
Azure resource roles and on-premises Active Directory groups only
Microsoft Entra roles, Azure resource roles, and PIM for Groups
Third-party SaaS application roles only

explanation: Correct: PIM covers Microsoft Entra roles, Azure resource roles, and PIM for Groups — the three manage options in the PIM blade. It does not manage SharePoint site permissions directly, does not manage on-premises AD group membership, and does not manage third-party SaaS roles.

prompt: An eligible administrator is about to activate the Privileged Role Administrator role. The role settings require MFA, justification, and approval. What must the activation include?

options.text: A written letter from the user's manager, filed with IT
Presence in the office on the corporate network
Approval only — MFA and justification cannot be required together
An MFA check, a business justification, and/or approval from designated approvers, as configured in the role settings

explanation: Correct: activation can require an MFA check, a business justification, or approval from designated approvers — and the role settings can require all three at once. It does not require a manager's written letter, does not require the user to be on-site, and does not skip MFA for eligible users.

prompt: An eligible administrator activates the Helpdesk Administrator role, which has no approval requirement. When can they start using it?

options.text: The member can start using the role immediately after activating it
The member must wait 24 hours for the activation to propagate
The member must get a second approval from a Global Administrator anyway
The member can use the role only after the next access review

explanation: Correct: if approval is not required, the member can start using the role as soon as they activate it — the activation is immediate. There is no waiting period, no automatic second approval, and no requirement to wait for a notification.

prompt: Your tenant has 40 permanent Global Administrators. Beyond alerts, how can PIM itself force a periodic check that each of them still needs the role?

options.text: PIM cannot review role assignments; only group memberships can be reviewed
Access reviews in PIM automatically convert permanent assignments to eligible ones
PIM supports access reviews of role assignments so reviewers can certify that users still need the roles
Access reviews in PIM only cover Azure resource roles, not Entra roles

explanation: Correct: PIM lets you conduct access reviews to ensure users still need roles — reviews of privileged role assignments are a core PIM capability, alongside audit history download. Access reviews do not convert assignments, do not delete roles, and are not limited to group membership.

prompt: Your tenant has Entra ID P1 only. You try to enable PIM for Groups on a role-assignable security group. What happens?

options.text: It works — PIM for Groups is included in P1
It works, but only for owner assignments, not member assignments
It works if the admin holds Global Administrator, regardless of licences
It is blocked — PIM requires Entra ID Governance licensing, which a P1-only tenant does not have

explanation: Correct: PIM requires licences — Entra ID Governance licensing — so a P1-only tenant cannot use PIM at all, for Entra roles, Azure roles, or groups. The limitation is licensing, not the role, not the group type, and not the admin's own role.

prompt: A system-assigned managed identity on a VM needs the Key Vault Secrets User role on one vault for a weekend migration. Can PIM manage that assignment?

options.text: Yes — PIM assignments can be made to managed identities as well as users, groups, and service principals
No — managed identities cannot hold any role assignment
Yes, but only as an eligible assignment, never as an active one
No — the managed identity must first be converted to a service principal

explanation: Correct: PIM can assign roles to managed identities as well as users, groups, and service principals — the automation identity can hold a role assignment like any other principal. The other options invent a limitation: managed identities are assignable principals in PIM, and the assignment does not need to be converted to a user assignment.

prompt: An administrator activates the User Administrator role for 4 hours, finishes the task in 1 hour, and leaves the role alone. What happens after 4 hours?

options.text: The role stays active until the user signs out
The role stays active until an approver revokes it
The activation expires after the preconfigured period and the user must activate again to continue
The role converts to a permanent active assignment after the first activation
